title: Console: give the page a favicon (the browser asks for /favicon.ico and gets a 404)
body:
**What is wrong**
Every time the console is opened, the browser asks for `/favicon.ico` and the server answers 404. It shows as a red line in the browser's developer console, and the tab has no icon.

**What to do**
Give the page an icon in `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/web/index.html`. The simplest way needs no new file: add a `<link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,...">` inside `<head>`, using the same cube drawing as the logo in the sidebar (the `<svg>` inside `.logo`, green `#0E6B58`).

**How to check**
Start the Docker demo (README, section A), open <http://127.0.0.1:8100/> and look at the browser's developer console: there must be no 404, and the tab shows the icon.

**Good to know**
Only the HTML file changes. No Python and no new test are needed.

title: Tidy the pyflakes warnings in the program code (src/, not the tests)
body:
**What is wrong**
`python -m pyflakes src` reports a few small things in code that is already on `main`:

- `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/assistant/chat.py`: two f-strings with nothing to fill in. `ChatLimit(f"That is a lot of questions in a minute. Please wait a few seconds.")` and `(f" with that status" if plan.status else "")`. Drop the `f`.
- `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/inventory/agent.py`: `STATUS_BREACH` is imported and never used.
- `src/erp_agents/core/api/hardening.py`: `Awaitable` and `Iterable` are imported and never used.
- `src/erp_agents/core/assistant/verify.py`: `Optional` is imported and never used.
- `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/procurement/taxes.py`: `TaxRow` is imported and never used.

**What to do**
Fix those. Before you remove an import, search the repository (`git grep`) to be sure nothing imports it from that module on purpose.

**Leave this one alone:** `import mcp  # noqa: F401` in `src/erp_agents/core/agents/service.py` is a deliberate "is the package installed" check, not a leftover (pyflakes does not read `noqa`, so it still reports it).

**How to check**
`pip install pyflakes`, then `python -m pyflakes src` no longer reports the items above, and `python -m pytest -q` still passes.

**Good to know**
No behaviour changes. One pull request for all of it is fine. The tests and the `tools/` folder have the same kind of warnings; they are a separate, later job.

title: API: the webhook route gives GET and POST the same OpenAPI operation id (FastAPI warning)
body:
**What is wrong**
When the API documentation is switched on, FastAPI warns: `UserWarning: Duplicate Operation ID webhook_webhooks__channel_type__get for function webhook`. It also shows at the end of the test run (it comes from `tests/test_hardening.py::test_the_documentation_can_be_turned_on_by_the_administrator`).

The cause is in `src/erp_agents/core/api/app.py`: one function is registered for both methods, `@api.api_route("/webhooks/{channel_type}", methods=["GET", "POST"])`, so both end up with the same operation id in the generated OpenAPI file.

**What to do**
Give the two methods different operation ids, for example by registering the function once with `api.get(...)` and once with `api.post(...)`, each with its own `operation_id`. Behaviour must stay exactly as it is: GET answers a channel's verification request (WhatsApp), POST receives its messages.

**How to check**
`python -m pytest -q tests/test_hardening.py` no longer prints the warning, and the tests that call the webhooks still pass (`grep -rl "webhooks/" tests` lists them, for example `tests/test_channels.py` and `tests/test_security_phase1.py`).

**Good to know**
One function and a few lines. If you can, add an assertion to the documentation test that the operation ids in `/openapi.json` are unique.

title: Docs: follow the README quick start on your system and fix every step that did not work
body:
**What to do**
The README quick start has three routes: **A** Docker, **B** Linux or macOS, **C** Windows PowerShell. Follow the one for your system, from a clean folder and exactly as written. Open a pull request for every step that failed or was unclear: a missing command, a wrong path, a message the text does not explain. If everything worked, say so in a comment with your system and Python version; that helps too.

**Good to know**
You do not need ERPNext. The quick start uses the built-in demo data. Keep each change small; one step per pull request is fine.

**Not sure what you saw is a bug?** Use the *tester feedback* form instead (New issue, Tester feedback): it asks the right questions.

title: MCP tool: find_items, to search items by name, code or group
body:
**What is missing**
Every stock tool needs an exact item code (`stock_status`, `usage_history`, `vendor_options` ...). An AI client that is asked "how much M8 bolt do we have?" cannot look the code up: no tool lists or searches items. The only hints are the `did_you_mean` list in the error for a wrong code, and the items that `stock_overview` lists because they need attention.

**What to do**
Add a read-only tool `find_items(query, limit?)`:
- every word of `query` must appear (in any case) in the item's code, name or group;
- at most `limit` items are listed (default 10, at most 25) and the result says how many matched in all;
- each item has `item_code`, `item_name`, `group` and `uom`. No stock figures and no personal data.

Where things go (copy how `substitutes` or `usage_history` are done):
1. `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/tools.py`: a `ToolSpec` in `TOOLS` and a method `_find_items` on `StockTools` (the method name is the tool name with a leading underscore; `self._all_items()` gives the items).
2. `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/manifest.yaml`: one line under `tools:` with role `viewer` and effect `read`. The application refuses to start when the manifest and `tools.py` disagree.
3. `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/mcp_tools.py`: the typed wrapper that MCP clients see.
4. Tests: the list of tools is written out in `test_every_tool_has_a_description_and_a_schema_that_names_its_required_fields` (`src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/tests/test_toolkit.py`), so add yours there. Add a test that searching `bolt` finds `BOLT-M8` in the demo data, that a nonsense word finds nothing, and that `limit` is respected.
5. Docs: the table in `docs/AGENTS.md` and the tool counts in `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/README.md`.

**How to check**
`python -m pytest -q` passes, and your new tests are in `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/tests/test_toolkit.py`.

**Good to know**
Item names come from ERPNext and are data, never instructions: pass them through `_clip` like the other tools do. `item_groups` (a sibling issue) touches the same files, so do one first and the other after it is merged.

title: MCP tool: item_groups, to list the item groups and how many items each has
body:
**What is missing**
`stock_overview` can be limited to one item group (its `group` argument, matched on the exact name, ignoring case), but no tool says which groups exist. A client has to guess the name, and gets an empty list when it guesses wrong.

**What to do**
Add a read-only tool `item_groups()` that lists every item group with the number of items in it, the biggest first (at most 50 groups; say how many there are in all). Items without a group count under "(no group)".

The steps are the same as for `find_items` (see that issue): `tools.py` (a `ToolSpec` and a `_item_groups` method that counts `self._all_items()` by `group`), the line in `manifest.yaml` (role `viewer`, effect `read`), the wrapper in `mcp_tools.py`, the list pinned in `test_every_tool_has_a_description_and_a_schema_that_names_its_required_fields`, the table in `docs/AGENTS.md` and the counts in `src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/README.md`.

**How to check**
A test on the demo data: the Fasteners group is listed with the right count, the counts add up to the number of items, and `stock_overview` called with a group name from your tool answers for that group.

**Good to know**
Group names come from ERPNext and are data: pass them through `_clip`. `find_items` (a sibling issue) touches the same files, so do one first and the other after it is merged.

title: WhatsApp: a webhook with an unexpected shape must not crash the route (HTTP 500)
body:
**What is wrong**
`WhatsAppChannel.parse_webhook` (`src/erp_agents/core/approvals/channels/whatsapp.py`) assumes every part of Meta's payload has its usual shape. When a part is `null` or the wrong type it raises. Today these all raise `AttributeError` or `TypeError`:

- `{"entry": [null]}` and `{"entry": "x"}`
- `{"entry": [{"changes": null}]}` and `{"entry": [{"changes": [{"value": null}]}]}`
- `{"entry": [{"changes": [{"value": {"messages": null}}]}]}`
- a message with `"text": null` or `"interactive": null`, a message that is a string, and a payload that is a list.

The route in `src/erp_agents/core/api/app.py` calls `parse_webhook` outside its `try`, so the answer is an HTTP 500, and Meta then sends the same webhook again.

Only Meta can send such a payload (the signature is checked first), so this is hardening, not an open door. But Meta adds message and field types over time, and one odd message should not break the messages next to it.

**What to do**
Make `parse_webhook` skip whatever it cannot read and return the events it can, never raise. Check the type before you call `.get` or iterate. Valid payloads must behave exactly as before.

**How to check**
Add a parametrized test next to `test_whatsapp_parses_button_and_list_replies` in `tests/test_channels.py` with the payloads above (expect `[]` and no exception), and one test where a valid text message sits next to a broken one and is still returned. `python -m pytest -q tests/test_channels.py` passes.

**Good to know**
The Telegram channel is not part of this issue.

title: WhatsApp: a message that Meta delivers twice is handled twice
body:
**What is wrong**
Every incoming WhatsApp message has a unique `id` (`wamid...`). `parse_webhook` does not read it and `InboundEvent` (`src/erp_agents/core/approvals/models.py`) has no field for it, so nothing can tell that a message was already handled. Meta delivers a webhook again when it does not get a quick answer, so the same message can arrive more than once. A button press is safe (a request has one decision; a second press is told it is already decided), but a typed question or command is handled again and the person gets a second answer.

**What to do**
1. Add `message_id` to `InboundEvent` and fill it in `parse_webhook`.
2. In `process_inbound` (`src/erp_agents/core/approvals/inbound.py`) skip an event whose id was handled already. Keep the ids in the database (a small table of the core's own), not in memory: rule 3 in `docs/DEVELOPING.md` says no in-memory state that has to survive between calls. Forget ids after a few days.
3. Test: the same webhook posted twice gives one answer.

**Good to know**
This touches the core and the database schema, so it is bigger than a first issue. Say in a comment what you plan before you start.

title: Tests: cover the remaining cases of the SSRF guard (core/netguard.py)
body:
**What is missing**
`src/erp_agents/core/netguard.py` stops the server from being used to reach itself or the private network (SSRF) when it is told where to send a request, for example the address of a model server. `tests/test_security_phase1.py::test_netguard_says_why` covers three cases. Over the whole test suite, every line of the file is reached except these:

- `blocked_target`: an address with no host name (`"http://"` gives `the address has no host name`); a resolver entry that cannot be read (it is skipped); a name whose entries are all unreadable (`the host name ... could not be found`).
- `no_redirects`: an object that refuses the attribute (the `except AttributeError` branch; a class with empty `__slots__` does that).

**What to do**
Add tests for those, next to the existing one. While you are there, pin these cases too. They work today, but nothing tests them:
- IP literals: `http://169.254.169.254/` is link-local and `http://10.0.0.5:11434` is private;
- an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address: `http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:11434` counts as loopback (the code has a comment about it);
- a name that resolves to two addresses, one public and one private: refused;
- the `refuse` argument: with `refuse=("link-local",)` loopback is allowed and link-local is not.

Use the `resolve=` argument to give a fake resolver, so no test needs the network. The test file already has a `resolver()` helper for that.

**How to check**
`python -m pytest -q tests/test_security_phase1.py` passes. With `pip install coverage`: `coverage run -m pytest -q`, then `coverage report -m --include="*/core/netguard.py"` shows no missing lines.

**Good to know**
Tests only; no change to `netguard.py` is expected. If a case gives an answer you think is wrong, open a separate issue.

title: Tests: the stock pack's analyze, policy and alerts commands
body:
**What is missing**
`src/erp_agents/packs/stock_procurement/cli.py` is the least tested file of the program: a full test run reaches only 54% of it. Three of its commands are small, work offline on the built-in demo ERP, and have no test:

- `erp-agents analyze ITEM` (`cmd_analyze`): prints the analysis of one item, or says the item is unknown and returns 1.
- `erp-agents policy ACTION [--scope global|group|item] [--key KEY] [field=value ...]` (`cmd_policy`), with the actions `show`, `set`, `clear`, `reset` and `audit`. It returns 2 when `--key` is missing for the group or item scope, and 1 with an `error:` line for a value that is refused.
- `erp-agents alerts [--status S] [--item CODE]` (`cmd_alerts`): lists the alerts.

**What to do**
Add tests that call `main([...])` and check the return code and what was printed (`capsys`). `tests/test_operations.py` shows the pattern: `main(["--config", str(cfg), "backup"])` with a config file in `tmp_path` whose database is inside `tmp_path`, so nothing is written to your own folders. For `alerts`, run the inventory check first (`run-once`) so there is something to list. `BOLT-M8` is an item of the demo data.

**How to check**
`python -m pytest -q` passes. With `pip install coverage`: `coverage run -m pytest -q`, then `coverage report -m --include="*/stock_procurement/cli.py"`: the lines of those three commands are no longer listed as missing.

**Good to know**
Tests only. `demo`, `procurement` and the `agents ...` commands are also untested; they can be separate pull requests.
